newsitem.title: USA: Senate strips all "killer" amendments from treaty.
newsitem.headline: Senate strips all "killer" amendments from treaty.

text.p: The U.S. Senate on Thursday cleared the way for a vote to approve a world treaty outlawing chemical weapons by stripping out four disputed conditions that would have prevented U.S. ratification.
In the last of a series of votes, it rejected, 66-34, a provision that would have forced changes in the treaty, which has already been ratified by 74 countries.

The changes concerned two articles on exchange of information between parties to the treaty and provision of chemical weapons defences that treaty opponents said would spur proliferation of poison gas instead of eliminating it.

President Bill Clinton had earlier given Senate Republican Leader Trent Lott assurances that if these articles led to proliferation or endangered U.S. security he would be prepared to withdraw from the treaty.

In earlier debate, the Senate rejected other so-called "killer" amendments that would have upgraded the standards of verification against cheating to a level that could not be met, made ratification conditional Russia's joining the pact, and barred ratification until countries like Iraq, Libya and North Korea had signed up.

It also rejected an amendment that would have barred nationals of countries designated as supporters of international terrorism from carrying out inspections of chemical facilities in the United States. This amendment was not regarded as a treaty "killer."
